summary: A. B. Gajendragadkar worked in Indology. He served as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad, and as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
A. C. Spearing studied at the University of Cambridge and Jesus College from around 1955 to 1960. He held a post at the University of Virginia from approximately 1987 to 2018.

A. Charles Muller specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned a PhD from Stony Brook University under Sung Bae Park and studied at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner, later holding professorships at Toyo Gakuen University and the University of Tokyo.

A. H. Armstrong studied philosophy at Jesus College from around 1928 to 1932. He held posts at Swansea University (~1936–1939), the University of Malta (~1939–1943), Cardiff University (~1946–1950), and the University of Liverpool (~1950–1972).

A. K. Ramanujan worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Mysore, Maharaja's College, and Indiana University. He held positions at Baroda College, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago (~1962–1993).
A. N. Krishna Aiyangar was an Indologist who served as Joint Editor of Brahmavidyā: The Adyar Library Bulletin (~1937–1944) and at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1937–1941).
A. N. Narasimhia was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held a post at the University of Mysore.
A. S. Gadre worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Hari Damodar Velankar and served as Director of Archaeology at the Baroda Museum and Picture Gallery.

A. V. Williams Jackson was an Indologist and Iranian specialist who studied at Columbia University under Edward Washburn Hopkins and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He was a professor at Columbia University (~1895–1935) and served the American Oriental Society.

A. W. Barber worked in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 under Robert J. Miller and Awadh Kishore Narain. He held a post at the University of Calgary around 1986.

Aaron P. Proffitt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback and Donald S. Lopez Jr., becoming an assistant professor at University at Albany, SUNY, around 2015.

Abdulaziz Sachedina worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1963–1967) and the University of Toronto (~1972–1976), and held a post at the University of Virginia from approximately 1976 to 2012.

Abdur Rehman worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned a PhD at Australian National University (~1973–1976) under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and Ahmad Hasan Dani, and became an assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Peshawar.

Abel Bergaigne was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michel Bréal (~1867–1869). He held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1888) and the University of Paris (~1877–1888).

Abigail I. MacBain specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University (~2006–2008), where she studied with Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, and Shayne Clarke, among others.

Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was an interpreter of oriental languages at the University of Paris in 1762 and a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1763–1805).
Abraham Zablocki works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Cornell University by around 2005 and held a post at Agnes Scott College around 2005.

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (~2001–2005) and was a research associate at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from 2004 to 2006.

Adalbert Bezzenberger worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, later holding a post at Göttingen from around 1874 to 1880.

Adalbert Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1833–1837). He later served as director of the Köllnisches Gymnasium from around 1870 to 1881.
